text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Opposition leaders from Nyanza province in western Kenya file a suit in court seeking to halt the ongoing voter registration exercise.
- Figures from the Electoral Commission indicate that some 5.1 million people may be registered as voters by this week.
- The coalition National Convention Assembly (NCA) calls on Kenyans to turn out in large numbers at parliament buildings ahead of the state budget speech late on Thursday.
- President Daniel arap Moi says the opposition is planning for chaos on Kenyatta Day (October 20), a public holiday that honours Kenya's freedom fighters.
- Nadya Balala, wife of exiled preacher Sheikh Khalid Balala pleads with the government to allow him back into the country.
- Nairobi City Council houses may go on sale any time, an assistant minister for local government says.
- Some 19 foreign envoys snub a meeting convened by the NCA seeking international support for constitutional reform demands.
